note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Qfin is the largest US-listed peer, with the same funding and collection exposure. It reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-24, after FINV last spoke on 08-27. Q3 loan volume was RMB49.5bn, -40.6% YoY. Revenue was RMB3.09bn, -13.4% QoQ. It guided Q4 non-GAAP net income to RMB250-350m (-67% to -77% YoY) and Q4 volume to about -20% QoQ. Management said liquidity will tighten further over the next one or two quarters as ABS issuance costs rise. It said regulatory uncertainty persists into 2027, the 30-day collection rate of 86% is near historic lows and will not return to 88%, and 'a 3% take rate is impossible to maintain' (FINV's own China take rate was about 3.2% in Q2). The read-through is that FINV's FY revenue guide (low end RMB11.5bn) and its Q4/2027 commentary are more likely to be cut or softened than reaffirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FINV trades on the guide. Q2 2026 (2026-08-27): the FY guide was steered to the low end and the stock fell about 15-19% (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/FinVolution+Group+Reports+Second+Quarter+2026+Financial+Results+and+Reaffirms+Full Year+Revenue+Guidance ; sweep row cites ainvest -15%). Q1 2026: the outlook was reaffirmed with a new US$150m buyback and the stock rose about 15% (sweep row, secondary). Q3 2025 (2025-11-20): -11% intraday, the largest fall since March 2023 (https://www.itiger.com/hant/news/2585151253).

findings.finding: From FINV's own Q2 call: China transaction volume was 'down around 50% in July'. China funding cost rose 30bp QoQ to 3.7% with another 30bp in July. Collection capacity 'took a bit of a hit' after the late-July regulatory action on collection, and early risk indicators were up about 20% versus Q2. The release said 'we anticipate a considerable contraction in transaction volume in China' for Q3. So the reported Q3 will show a deep China volume drop, rising funding costs and worse early credit. All of this sits inside what the company already told the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported-quarter lines have not decided FINV's last prints; the guide has (see the first finding). In Q2 2026, revenue up 6% QoQ and net profit up 1% QoQ did not stop a 15-19% fall on the guide.

findings.finding: FINV's FY guide low end already builds in a severe H2. H1 revenue was about RMB6.61bn (Q2 RMB3,403m, Q1 about 3,210m), so the RMB11.5bn low end needs only about RMB4.89bn in H2, about 2.44bn a quarter, or -28% against Q2. Qfin's revenue fell only 13.4% QoQ on a roughly 22% QoQ volume drop (Q2 63.4bn to Q3 49.5bn), because facilitation revenue lags volume. On that basis FINV can plausibly hold or narrowly touch the low end even after a 50% July China volume drop, so a reaffirmed low end is a live outcome, not a remote one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time the guide was reaffirmed outright (Q1 2026, with a buyback), the stock rose about 15% (sweep row). Steering to the low end (Q2) fell 15-19%. A hold of the low end from a 52-week low after a peer's shock guide is untested.

findings.finding: Capital return headroom: FINV held cash of RMB3.26bn plus short-term investments of RMB3.16bn (about US$946m) at 2026-06-30, with leverage of 2.1x 'around historic lows'. Its fifth buyback program, up to US$150m, runs 2026-05-30 to 2028-05-29, and only US$27.4m was repurchased in Q2. The dividend policy pays 20-30% of prior-year net income. With the ADS at a 52-week low of $2.33, Q3 repurchase pace or a step-up/new authorisation at the print is a lever. The counterweight is that Qfin said on 11-24 it will take a 'more prudent approach to capital deployment', so FINV may slow buybacks rather than speed them up. The size is net of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: the new US$150m buyback with a reaffirmed guide gave about +15% (sweep row, secondary), with the buyback and the guide not separable.

findings.finding: Indonesia (more than 50% of FINV overseas volume and revenue; overseas was 27% of group revenue in Q2) worsened in Q3. OJK data put industry fintech-lending TWP90 at 5.36% in September 2026, against 4.32% in July and 2.82% a year earlier. Industry outstanding slipped from Rp106.94tn (August) to Rp106.48tn (September). Net of the company: AdaKami self-reports a 0% TWP90 and loan rejections as its top complaint, and part of the industry spike is attributed to two fraud-hit platforms. The 30% debt-to-income cap also limits growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Overseas growth was the positive leg in the Q2 release (overseas operating profit more than doubled, unique borrowers +130%) and did not offset the guide-driven fall.

findings.finding: Relative position in the sector: smaller peers were already loss-making or guiding to losses. Jiayin posted a Q2 2026 net loss of RMB183.6m on RMB9.5bn of volume, and LexinFintech guided Q3 to a possible net loss. FINV earned RMB427m in Q2 with 90+ DPD of 2.10% and leverage of 2.1x. Qfin also said it expects smaller, lower-compliance platforms to exit and competition for customers to ease. So FINV printing a profitable Q3 in a contracting market is a relative-strength point that a shakeout could support.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed separately. Relative resilience did not protect the stock in Q2 2026.

outside_window.finding: LexinFintech reports Q3 2026 after the US close on 2026-12-03, a further sector read that is too late for this window.

Regulatory path: on-balance-sheet lending must be priced at 4x LPR by end-2027, and further rules on market entry, partnership models and funding supply are under consideration (Qfin call). This weighs on the 2027 take rate beyond this window, except as far as FINV's own call commentary reflects it.

findings.finding: Grupo Supervielle, the first of the four Argentine bank ADRs to report Q3 2026 (story dated 2026-11-17), printed net income of ARS6.8bn, about half of Q2's ARS13.6bn, ROAE 2.2%. Net financial income fell 22.4% QoQ and NIM fell 430bp to 16%. EPS was $0.08 against a $0.16 consensus, and 2026 ROE guidance was cut for the fourth straight quarter, to 1-2% reported and 5-6% adjusted. Offsets in the same print: NPL improved to 5.4%, loan-loss provisions fell 14.5% QoQ, and opex fell 26.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No dated record of BMA's reaction to a peer's print. On Macro's own prints the margin line drove the Q4 2025 miss (-7.3% ADR with the sector) and the Q2 2026 beat (muted).

findings.finding: Asset quality is turning in the system data Macro's Q3 will mirror. BCRA September 2026: private-sector NPL fell 0.25pp to 7.50%; household NPL fell 0.61pp to 12.20%, its second monthly decline; the irregular balance fell 2.58% real, the first negative since April 2024; estimated PD fell a fourth month to 2.04%; provision coverage rose to 88.2%. Macro guided NPL to 5.5-6% by year end from 6.25% in Q2, and its book is consumer-heavy (consumer NPL 8.42% in Q2), where the improvement is concentrated. The system figure is helped by write-offs and refinancing (households refinanced 3.9% of the book; 24.1% of irregular balances refinanced).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NPL was the line analysts flagged after Q2 2026 (SBS: 'monitoring delinquency will be essential'; NPL 6.25% from 5.4%) when the local share went -2.2% then +1.8% (https://www.iprofesional.com/finanzas/462851-que-hacer-con-las-acciones-de-banco-macro-tras-su-balance). In Q2 2026 Galicia printed lower loan-loss charges and its ADR still fell (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/latinoamerica/argentina/galicia-sale-del-rojo-y-destaca-menor-cargo-por-incobrabilidad-pero-acciones-ceden-en-wall-street/).

findings.finding: Q2 2026 net income of RMB47.0m carried two items that will not repeat. One was a reversal of earlier guarantee reserves, which the CFO said is not 'a new lower run rate for the provision'. The other was a RMB95.3m provision for credit losses on deposits, against RMB0.7m a year earlier, which writes off guarantee money one funding institution has not returned; management said it may still come back. So Q3 net income against Q2 depends on two below-the-line items. A recovery of the guarantee money would reverse up to RMB95m; a normal guarantee provision would cut Q3 profit.
